summary: Build a distributed scientific or data-processing application with a measurable scaling boundary and a tested failure-recovery story.
outcomes: Design a complete multi-GPU data and communication path.
Explain scaling, reliability and cost with reproducible evidence.
sequence: Choose a simulation or data workload and define success and reference behavior.
Partition work, communication and input pipelines across devices.
Profile bottlenecks and test a controlled failure.
Publish scaling, recovery and cost/energy results with constraints.

visual.question: What becomes the bottleneck as device count increases?
visual.interaction: Compare recorded scales and inject an illustrative rank failure into the state diagram.

practice.task: Deliver a two-or-more-device project or clearly labeled trace-based study when hardware is unavailable.
practice.success: Correctness, scaling and recovery evidence are separate; simulated results are never presented as measured GPU runs.
